summary: OpenReader is a self-hosted document reader that converts text files, EPUBs, PDFs, DOCX documents, and Markdown notes into speech. It allows you to listen to documents in real time using text-to-speech engines or export them as audiobooks.
goodFor: It suits individuals who want to convert their personal document libraries into audio formats or listen to reading materials on private infrastructure.
watchOut: High-quality text-to-speech processing can be resource-intensive, requiring adequate hardware depending on the TTS engines utilised.
deployNotes: As a Docker-based application, you will typically need to configure persistent volume mounts to retain your document library and generated audio files, alongside a reverse proxy for HTTPS.
